title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a Grothendieck manuscript page. It is page 6 of a typewritten English text (archive folio 87, written in by hand) by Dennis Sullivan, from the circulated preprint or lecture version of his rational homotopy theory, c. 1973–75, which became 'Infinitesimal computations in topology' (Publ. IHÉS 47, 1977). Grothendieck kept it among his notes for the 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power de Rham complex.

Modern content:
(1) The inductive construction is finished. One adds generators degree by degree to kill cohomology defects. This gives a minimal Sullivan algebra (ΛV, d) with a quasi-isomorphism ρ: (ΛV, d) → E, where E is the de Rham algebra (in the simplicial case, piecewise polynomial or smooth forms). Minimality means d(V) ⊂ Λ^{≥2}V.
(2) Theorem B concerns a simply connected triangulated space X, with finite type implicitly assumed:
- (i) dim π_i(X)⊗Q = dim V^i.
- (ii) The rank of the rational Hurewicz map π_i X → H_i X equals dim(V^i ∩ ker d). Dually, the d-closed generators are exactly the indecomposable cohomology classes that pair nontrivially with spherical classes.
- (iii) The quadratic part d_1: V → Λ²V of the differential is dual, up to sign and degree-shift conventions, to the Whitehead product on π_*(X)⊗Q.
(3) The proof sketch is a rational Postnikov induction. Each stage is an elementary extension (ΛV_{<n} ⊗ ΛV^n, d), modelling a principal K(π_n⊗Q, n)-fibration. The text attributes the method to Hirsch's de Rham computation of the cohomology of principal bundles (the 'Hirsch extension'), suggested by Thom in the 1954 Cartan Seminar. Graded commutativity of the wedge product is essential.
(4) Consequently the minimal model directly encodes the rational Postnikov tower.

Relevance to the surrounding notes: on the neighbouring pages Grothendieck studies cochain functors C^n on simplicial sets that send colimits to limits. Such functors are representable by simplicial objects C^n_•, which must be resolutions of M. This is exactly the formal structure behind Sullivan's simplicial algebra of polynomial forms ∇(p,*) on Δ_p. It is also the structure behind the search for an integral, divided-power replacement for it, which is the theme of the 1976 talk.
errors: No mathematical error at the level of a survey statement. Implicit hypotheses are omitted: finite type (finite rational Betti numbers) and coefficients in Q (or R). 'Rank' means dimension after tensoring with Q.
'Guy Hirsh' is a misspelling of Guy Hirsch in the typescript itself; the next line spells it 'Hirsch' correctly.
In (iii) the correspondence between the quadratic part of d and Whitehead products holds only up to sign and degree-shift conventions (dual of the Samelson/Whitehead Lie bracket on π_{*}(ΩX)⊗Q).

missed.claim: Archival evidence that Grothendieck owned and studied a pre-publication typescript of Sullivan's minimal-model text around 1975–76. He filed it among his notes on cochain functors on simplicial sets and on divided-power de Rham complexes. This documents a direct line from Sullivan's rational theory to Grothendieck's attempt at an integral or divided-power de Rham model for homotopy types, a theme he later raised in Pursuing Stacks. The page itself contains no new mathematics by Grothendieck.
missed.quote: The proof of theorem B shows the model can be used to directly construct the rational Postnikov system
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest for the prehistory of integral models of homotopy types (E∞ cochains in Mandell's work, divided-power or Cartan-type models). It shows Grothendieck engaging with Sullivan's theory at that time, which may be relevant for dating and contextualising his IHÉS talk.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a copy of Sullivan's well-known published results (minimal models, Theorem B), not Grothendieck's own work. Only the archival context, Grothendieck reading Sullivan's preprint, is mildly interesting.
transcription_corrections: Top right shows a handwritten '87' (archive foliation) next to the typed page number '6'.
The typescript itself reads 'Guy Hirsh' (sic) and later 'Hirsch'; the transcription is faithful.
In 'π_i X → H_i X' the subscripts are i (rendered with a typewriter-style subscript); the transcription is correct.
